text: The Chutak Hydroelectric Plant is a run-of-the-river power project situated on the Suru River, a tributary of the Indus, in the Kargil district of the Indian union territory of Ladakh. The barrage is located at Sarze village, and the powerhouse is situated on the right bank of the Suru near Chutak village. Construction of the project commenced on 23 September 2006, with the first three generators commissioned in November 2012 and the fourth commissioned in January 2013. The project features a 47.5-metre-long (156 ft) barrage, 15 m high above the crest level, an underground powerhouse, a 3.3 m diameter and 10.02 km long head race tunnel, and four vertical Francis turbines of 11 MW each. It utilizes a gross head of 63.4 m (208 ft) to generate 216.41 GWh in a 90% dependable year, with an installed capacity of 44 MW. Each 11 MW generating unit is designed to operate under a rated head of 52 m and a rated discharge of 24.05 cubic metres per second. The barrage diverts water, resulting in a flooding area of only 0.135 km² (0.052 sq mi), yielding a high power density of 44 MW per 0.135 km², equivalent to 326 W/m², which is significantly higher than that of dam-based hydroelectric projects. The plant will be connected to the Northern Grid via the 220 kV Leh-Srinagar transmission line, scheduled for commissioning alongside the project’s commissioning. The project was developed by M/s National Hydroelectric Power Corporation Ltd., with the generating equipment supplied, erected, and commissioned by M/s Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL). The turbines were manufactured by BHEL's Bhopal unit, and the controls were supplied by BHEL's Bangalore unit, while the erection and commissioning were carried out by BHEL's Power Sector. As of the latest available information, all four generating units are operating successfully. The Chutak Hydroelectric Plant, along with the Nimoo Bazgo Hydroelectric Plant, was certified as compliant with the Indus Waters Treaty by the Indian Central Water Commission, and the project details were shared with Pakistan.
